memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They are to stay in that city until they have stood trial before the assembly and until the death of the high priest who is serving at that time. Then they may go back to their own home in the town from which they fled." - Josh 20:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The law of refuge held a striking detail: the one who had fled was to remain in the city of refuge until the death of the high priest who was serving at that time. Only then could they return freely to their own home. The death of the high priest marked the moment of the fugitive's full release. Their freedom was tied to the passing of the one who held that sacred office.

This is one of those quiet Old Testament pictures that shines brightly once we see Christ in it. The manslayer's release came through the death of the high priest. And for us, our full and final release from the guilt and penalty of sin comes through the death of our great High Priest, Jesus. Hebrews presents Jesus as the High Priest who offered Himself once for all, and through whose death we are set free (Heb 9:11-12, 15). The death that liberates us is His.

What a gospel this points to. The fugitive waited for a death that would open the way home; we look back to a death already accomplished that has opened our way to God forever. Because our High Priest has died — and risen — we are not merely sheltered temporarily but set free completely, welcomed home to the Father. The city of refuge sheltered until the high priest died; Christ our High Priest has died, and in Him we are released, forgiven, and brought home for good.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does it move you that the fugitive's release came through the high priest's death?
- How does Jesus, our great High Priest, secure your full release from sin?
- What does it mean to be not merely sheltered but set completely free in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, my great High Priest, thank You that through Your death I am not only sheltered but fully set free. Because You died and rose, I am forgiven and brought home to the Father. Amen.
